subject: Mythology
title: The Dagda: Father of the Gods
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Dagda: Father of the Gods.

hook.text: The Dagda was king of the Irish gods, a huge man who carried a club so heavy it needed wheels to move.

buildup.text: One end of his club killed the living. The other end brought the dead back to life with a single touch.

discovery.text: He owned a magic cauldron that never emptied and a harp that could control the seasons and human emotions.

twist.text: Despite his power, the Dagda was portrayed as a comical figure: fat, clumsy, and always eating too much.

climax.text: This mix of supreme power and earthy humor made him uniquely Celtic — a god you could laugh with and fear.

punchline.text: The most powerful god in Ireland was also the funniest.

quiz.question: What was special about the Dagda's club?
options: It could control the weather and summon storms
One end killed the living and the other revived the dead
It grew larger with each enemy defeated
